title: Why a16z's Martin Casado Believes the AI Boom Still Has Years to Run

reader_summary.headline: If you ask me, what is the one area that AI has surprised you?
reader_summary.overview: If you ask me, what is the one area that AI has surprised you? I've been developing my whole light and I would never have guessed it'd be this good. You have mentioned that some of the energy that you're seeing in AI really reminds you of the 90s.com boom.

key_points.text: This feels a lot like early 96, but I don't think we're anywhere close to late 90s level bubble.
key_points.evidence_quote: This feels a lot like early 96, but I don't think we're anywhere close to late 90s level bubble.

key_points.text: The current technology wave is you can actually deploy capital and you can get revenue on the other side of it.
key_points.evidence_quote: The current technology wave is you can actually deploy capital and you can get revenue on the other side of it.

key_points.text: And I think that is what the market is trying to normalize.
key_points.evidence_quote: And I think that is what the market is trying to normalize.

key_points.text: But there's a true value being created in the AI and I think that money's not falling.

thesis: The episode explores Martín Casado's perspective on the AI boom, arguing that the current technology wave allows for capital deployment and revenue generation, distinguishing it from a bubble while suggesting it could become the greatest super cycle in the last 20 years. The discussion also covers his market-first investing style, his background in game engines and simulations, and the potential of AI coding as a multi-trillion dollar opportunity.
